transcript.en: Good evening everyone. My name's Jon and I run Veg Out, a street food business selling vegan food.
transcript.zh: 晚上好，各位。我叫Jon，我经营着一家名为Veg Out的街头美食业务，销售纯素食品。

transcript.en: Since 2012 I've been travelling all around the country cooking vegan food in my converted van and selling it at all kinds of outdoor events.
transcript.zh: 自从2012年以来，我一直在全国各地驾驶改装的厢式货车烹饪纯素食品，并在各种户外活动中出售。

transcript.en: I'm here to give you some advice based on my experience.
transcript.zh: 我在这里给你一些基于我经验的建议。

transcript.en: The good news is that there's never been a better time to start your own street food business.
transcript.zh: 好消息是，现在正是创办街头小吃生意的最佳时机。

transcript.en: Street food continues to grow in popularity.
transcript.zh: 街头食品继续受到欢迎。

transcript.en: I think there are a couple of reasons for this.
transcript.zh: 我认为有几方面的原因。

transcript.en: The first is that street food is a reaction against fast food.
transcript.zh: 第一个是街头食品是对快餐的一种反应。

transcript.en: Street food ranges from high quality burgers to vegan curries and everything in between.
transcript.zh: 街头食品从高质量的汉堡到素食咖喱，各种各样的都有。

transcript.en: But while fast food is cheap and easy to find, it's not particularly good for you.
transcript.zh: 但是，虽然快餐既便宜又容易找到，但它对你的健康并不是特别好。

transcript.en: It's also the same everywhere.
transcript.zh: 而且，它在各个地方都是一样的。

transcript.en: What you get with street food on the other hand is something different.
transcript.zh: 而街头小吃则提供了一种不同的东西。

transcript.en: People like the idea of trying something they can't get anywhere else.
transcript.zh: 人们喜欢尝试那些在其他地方都找不到的东西的想法。

transcript.en: They also like seeing food prepared in front of them and which hasn't come straight out of a freezer.
transcript.zh: 他们也喜欢看到食物在他们面前被制作，而且没有直接从冷冻柜里拿出来。

transcript.en: You need to think about the best place to sell your street food.
transcript.zh: 你需要考虑一下最佳的地点来出售你的街头小吃。

transcript.en: People always think music festivals are an obvious place to start but the cost of renting a space can be huge.
transcript.zh: 人们总是认为音乐节是开始的好地方，但租场地的成本可能非常高。

transcript.en: And there's always a lot of competition.
transcript.zh: 而且总是有很多竞争。

transcript.en: Food markets, on the other hand, are great because customers are always really interested in food and give great feedback.
transcript.zh: 另一方面，食品市场很棒，因为顾客总是对食物很感兴趣，并给出很好的反馈。

transcript.en: And if you can get a spot in your local park – fantastic.
transcript.zh: 而且如果你能在当地的公园里得到一个位置——太棒了。

transcript.en: Usually very relaxed but with lots of customers passing by.
transcript.zh: 通常很放松，但有很多顾客路过。

transcript.en: Once you get established you'll start getting asked to do parties – which can be really challenging but lots of fun.
transcript.zh: 一旦你开始经营，你就会被邀请参加派对——这可能会很具有挑战性，但也很有趣。

transcript.en: Having street food at weddings has become quite fashionable too – but you need to really know what you're doing as everything needs to be perfect.
transcript.zh: 吃街边小吃在婚礼上也变得很流行——但你得真的知道怎么做，因为一切都得完美无缺。

transcript.en: Setting up a street food business costs a lot less than opening a restaurant or café but you'll have to buy some basic equipment.
transcript.zh: 开一个街头小吃的生意比开一家餐馆或咖啡馆要便宜得多，但你得买一些基本的设备。

transcript.en: I'd try to get things like hobs and fridges second hand if you can.
transcript.zh: 如果你能的话，试着买二手的炉子和冰箱。

transcript.en: You can replace them with better quality stuff if your business takes off.
transcript.zh: 如果生意发展起来，你可以换成更好的东西。

transcript.en: Renting is another option but you'll end up spending more money rather than saving it.
transcript.zh: 租赁也是一个选择，但你最终会花更多的钱而不是节省。

transcript.en: You've probably got a good idea about the food you're planning to sell.
transcript.zh: 你大概对打算卖什么食物已经有了一些想法。

transcript.en: I expect you've done some research to find out if anyone else is selling a similar product.
transcript.zh: 我预计你已经做了些研究，看看别人是否在卖类似的产品。

transcript.en: And you'll have thought about any possible allergies to nuts or eggs etc.
transcript.zh: 你肯定考虑过可能对坚果或鸡蛋等食物过敏的人吧。

transcript.en: But there's one thing people don't always think about and that's how you're going to serve it.
transcript.zh: 但有一件事人们往往不会想到，那就是你打算怎么提供它。

transcript.en: On a plate? In a bag? Will you provide a fork?
transcript.zh: 放在盘子里？装在袋子里？你会提供叉子吗？

transcript.en: Will it all be easily recyclable or reusable?
transcript.zh: 所有的东西都容易回收或重复使用吗？

transcript.en: It's got to be easy to eat and look attractive or customers won't come back.
transcript.zh: 食物要容易吃并且看起来有吸引力，否则顾客就不会再来了。

transcript.en: Once you get started, you should be prepared for things to go wrong.
transcript.zh: 一旦你开始，你应该准备好遇到问题。

transcript.en: Every business faces problems and here are a few examples from street food businesses that I know.
transcript.zh: 每一家企业都会遇到问题，这里有一些我了解的街头食品企业的例子。

transcript.en: My friends who run Thai Basil started by juggling their street food business with their day jobs in a restaurant.
transcript.zh: 我的朋友们经营的泰国薄荷，他们开始时是同时经营着餐馆的工作和街头食品生意。

transcript.en: Their work-life balance was non-existent as they were working til midnight in the restaurant all week and then took their food truck to markets on their days off.
transcript.zh: 他们的工作与生活平衡是非存在的，因为一周内他们每周都工作到午夜，然后在休息日将他们的货车带到市场。

transcript.en: The owners of Basque found it was hard to make a profit because the price of fish – essential for some of their dishes – was so high.
transcript.zh: Basque 的老板发现很难赚钱，因为鱼的价格非常高，这是他们一些菜肴的重要组成部分。

transcript.en: And it was hard to charge customers a lot more for those dishes.
transcript.zh: 而且很难让顾客为那些菜肴支付更高的价格。

transcript.en: So they had to stop focussing on fish dishes and include more vegetarian food.
transcript.zh: 因此他们不得不停止专注于鱼菜肴，而更多地包括素食食物。

transcript.en: The owners of Lou's kitchen were making salads to order from their van and some of their dishes were quite complicated.
transcript.zh: Lou‘s Kitchen 的老板正在他们的货车里制作沙拉，并且他们的一些菜肴相当复杂。

transcript.en: At one of their first events they ended up with people standing in a long queue for more than 15 minutes – and many of them lost patience.
transcript.zh: 他们第一次举办活动时，结果顾客排起了长长的队伍，等待时间超过 15 分钟，许多人失去了耐心。

transcript.en: So make sure whatever you offer can be served quickly and efficiently.
transcript.zh: 所以确保你提供的东西能够快速且高效地服务。

transcript.en: The owners of Chip Chop had found a perfect venue near a beach where there weren't any other street food trucks.
transcript.zh: Chip Chop 的主人发现了一个完美的场地，靠近海滩，那里没有其他流动食品车。

transcript.en: But what they hadn't realised was that they'd need a special licence – which individual businesses don't need at markets or festivals.
transcript.zh: 但他们没有意识到的是，他们需要一个特殊的许可证——而个体企业在市场或节日里不需要这样的许可证。

transcript.en: It was a complicated process and in the end they gave up.
transcript.zh: 这是一项复杂的过程，最后他们放弃了。

transcript.en: So I hope that's given you a flavour of ….
transcript.zh: 所以我希望这已经给你...
